- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to reflect downward pressure.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days), especially when sentiment is positive — apply a 5-10% downward correction to prevent overreaction.
- In early forecast windows (e.g., 30d with recent history), model shows persistent mean reversion bias — adjust by adding 1-2% to forecast if recent price is below 30-day average.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3-5 days, model often fails to adjust quickly — apply a lag correction: reduce forecast by 2-5% for the next 3-5 days.
- When sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model tends to overreact — suppress forecast growth by 1-3% to avoid false momentum.
